Current official PDF.js docs present the **generic build as a browser-oriented prebuilt package**: the getting-started page says the prebuilt package “includes the generic build of PDF.js and the viewer,” and its examples page says its main tutorial shows use “in a web browser.” https://mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/getting_started/ https://mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/examples/

The same official examples page says there are separate `examples/node/` examples for Node.js usage. https://mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/examples/

That example loads a document with `getDocument({ url: pdfPath })`, gets each page with `getPage(i)`, calls `await pdfPage.getTextContent()`, and prints `items.map(item => item.str).join(" ")`. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/examples/node/getinfo.mjs

**Supported fact**

Current official PDF.js docs present the **generic build as a browser-oriented prebuilt package**: the getting-started page says the prebuilt package “includes the generic build of PDF.js and the viewer,” and its examples page says its main tutorial shows use “in a web browser.” https://mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/getting_started/ https://mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/examples/

The same official examples page says there are separate `examples/node/` examples for Node.js usage. https://mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/examples/

The current official Node text-extraction example does **not** import the generic build; it imports `pdfjs-dist/legacy/build/pdf.mjs`. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/examples/node/getinfo.mjs

That example loads a document with `getDocument({ url: pdfPath })`, gets each page with `getPage(i)`, calls `await pdfPage.getTextContent()`, and prints `items.map(item => item.str).join(" ")`. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/examples/node/getinfo.mjs

The public API docs say `PDFPageProxy.getTextContent()` returns a promise for a `TextContent` object, and that all whitespace is normalized to standard spaces (`0x20`). https://mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/api/draft/module-pdfjsLib-PDFPageProxy.html

The `TextContent` docs say it contains an `items` array plus `styles`; `TextItem.str` is the text string, and `TextItem` also carries direction, transform, width, height, font name, and `hasEOL`. https://mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/api/draft/module-pdfjsLib.html

For Node-like environments, the current source explicitly warns: `Please use the legacy build in Node.js environments.` https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/display/node_utils.js

The current FAQ says PDF.js ships a default non-polyfilled build for the latest browsers and a separate `legacy` build for older environments; in its support table, `Node.js 22+` appears under the `legacy` build as “Mostly” supported with “Limited” automated testing. Bun is not listed in that table. https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/wiki/frequently-asked-questions

The runtime defaults in `src/display/api.js` are environment-sensitive. In Node.js, `useWorkerFetch` defaults to `false`, `isOffscreenCanvasSupported` defaults to `false`, `isImageDecoderSupported` defaults to `false`, `disableFontFace` defaults to `true`, and `useSystemFonts` defaults to `false` unless overridden. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/display/api.js

The same file defaults `ownerDocument` to `globalThis.document`. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/display/api.js

In a generic build detected as Node.js, PDF.js switches its default factories to `NodeCanvasFactory`, `NodeFilterFactory`, and `NodeBinaryDataFactory`. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/display/api.js

`node_utils.js` shows what those Node defaults assume at runtime: it uses `process.getBuiltinModule("module").createRequire(...)`, tries to load `@napi-rs/canvas`, polyfills `DOMMatrix` and `Path2D` from that package when possible, synthesizes a minimal `navigator` if `navigator.language` is missing, and reads local files through `fs/promises.readFile`. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/display/node_utils.js

For worker setup, the API source says `GlobalWorkerOptions.workerSrc` “should always be set,” and `PDFWorker` creates a module worker with `new Worker(workerSrc, { type: "module" })`; in generic builds it also uses `window.location` for same-origin handling. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/display/worker_options.js https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/display/api.js

The current API source also uses modern globals/features such as `Promise.withResolvers()` and `structuredClone(...)`. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/display/api.js

**Inference**

From those official sources, the **documented path outside the browser is “use the legacy build,” not “use the generic build.”** That inference follows from the Node example importing `legacy/build/pdf.mjs`, the explicit Node warning in `node_utils.js`, and the FAQ support table listing Node.js only under `legacy`. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/examples/node/getinfo.mjs https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/display/node_utils.js https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/wiki/frequently-asked-questions

For **text extraction only**, PDF.js appears less dependent on canvas rendering than for image rendering, because the official example extracts text with `getTextContent()` and only reads `item.str`; however, that is still an inference about practical portability, not an explicit Bun guarantee. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/examples/node/getinfo.mjs https://mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/api/draft/module-pdfjsLib-PDFPageProxy.html

For **Bun compatibility**, the most relevant runtime assumptions documented by current official sources are: a Node-style `process` object, `process.getBuiltinModule`, `createRequire`, file-system access, optional `@napi-rs/canvas` integration, browser-ish globals such as `document`, `navigator`, `Worker`, and `window.location`, plus modern JS globals like `Promise.withResolvers` and `structuredClone`. If Bun diverges on any of those behaviors, the generic build could fail or fall back in ways the docs do not promise to support. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/shared/util.js https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/display/node_utils.js https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/display/api.js https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/display/worker_options.js

**Uncertainty / lack of good evidence**

I found **no official PDF.js documentation in the sources above that explicitly says Bun is supported, unsupported, or tested**. The closest official support statement I found names `Node.js 22+` under the `legacy` build and does not mention Bun. https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/wiki/frequently-asked-questions

I also found **no official source here that recommends the generic build for Bun specifically**. The available official material points to browser use for the generic build and to the legacy build for Node-style environments. https://mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/examples/ https://mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/getting_started/ https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/display/node_utils.js

**Disagreement**

I do not see a hard contradiction in the official sources, but there is a practical tension: the project distributes a generic prebuilt package, yet its current official Node guidance and runtime warning both steer non-browser usage toward the `legacy` build. https://mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/getting_started/ https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/examples/node/getinfo.mjs https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/display/node_utils.js

# PDFWorker Node.js Handling

The code shows PDFWorker disables web workers in Node.js environments. Here are the relevant portions:

**Worker Disabling in Node.js:**
```javascript
if (isNodeJS) {
  // Workers aren't supported in Node.js, force-disabling them there.
  this.#isWorkerDisabled = true;
  GlobalWorkerOptions.workerSrc ||= PDFJSDev.test("LIB")
    ? "../pdf.worker.js"
    : "./pdf.worker.mjs";
}
```

**Fake Worker Setup:**
When standard workers aren't available, the code invokes `#setupFakeWorker()`, which loads worker code into the main thread via dynamic import:

```javascript
const worker = typeof PDFJSDev === "undefined"
  ? await import("pdfjs/pdf.worker.js")
  : await __raw_import__(this.workerSrc);
```

The fake worker uses a `LoopbackPort` for internal messaging rather than actual worker threads. This approach allows PDF.js to function in Node.js despite the absence of native web worker support.

**Key Comment:**
The code states: "Workers aren't supported in Node.js, force-disabling them there," indicating deliberate design to handle this platform limitation by falling back to main-thread execution.

# PDF.js hors navigateur, extraction de texte et hypothèses d'exécution (impact Bun)

## 1. Faits documentés par les sources officielles

**Builds : `generic` vs `generic-legacy`**
- Le README du dépôt indique que `npx gulp generic` regroupe les fichiers de `src/` en scripts de production et construit le viewer générique ; `npx gulp generic-legacy` produit les mêmes fichiers dans `build/generic-legacy/build/`. Les deux produisent `pdf.js` et `pdf.worker.js`, mais « only `pdf.js` needs to be included since `pdf.worker.js` will be loaded by `pdf.js` » ([README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/README.md)).
- Le README de `pdfjs-dist` précise que le dossier `legacy/` est destiné « for usage with older browsers or environments, without support for modern features such as optional chaining, nullish coalescing, and private `class` fields/methods » ([pdfjs-dist README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdfjs-dist/master/README.md)). Le mot **« environments »** est ce qui rattache explicitement le build legacy aux runtimes non-navigateur.
- Le code n'est activé pour Node que dans le build GENERIC : `isNodeJS` est défini comme `(typeof PDFJSDev === "undefined" || PDFJSDev.test("GENERIC")) && typeof process === "object" && process + "" === "[object process]" && !process.versions.nw && !(process.versions.electron && process.type && process.type !== "browser")` ([src/shared/util.js](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/shared/util.js)). Autrement dit, **seul le build générique (ou legacy générique) contient les chemins de code Node**.

**Exemples officiels hors navigateur**
- Les exemples Node officiels sont `examples/node/getinfo.mjs` et `examples/node/pdf2png/` ([arborescence](https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/tree/master/examples/node)), également référencés depuis la page d'exemples ([mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/examples](https://mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/examples/)) et le wiki « Setup PDF.js in a website » ([wiki](https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/wiki/Setup-PDF.js-in-a-website)).
- Les deux importent **le build legacy en ESM** : `import { getDocument } from "pdfjs-dist/legacy/build/pdf.mjs"` ([getinfo.mjs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/examples/node/getinfo.mjs), [pdf2png.mjs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/examples/node/pdf2png/pdf2png.mjs)).
- `pdf2png.mjs` lit le fichier via `new Uint8Array(fs.readFileSync(pdfPath))` et configure explicitement `cMapUrl` / `standardFontDataUrl` ; le rendu passe par une canvas factory puis `canvasAndContext.canvas.toBuffer("image/png")` ([pdf2png.mjs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/examples/node/pdf2png/pdf2png.mjs)).

**Extraction de texte**
- Schéma officiel dans `getinfo.mjs` : `getDocument(...).promise` → `getMetadata()` → boucle sur les pages → `page.getTextContent()` → concaténation des `item.str` → `page.cleanup()` ([getinfo.mjs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/examples/node/getinfo.mjs)).
- L'API documente `getTextContent(params)` → `Promise<TextContent>`, avec la mise en garde : « All occurrences of whitespace will be replaced by standard spaces (0x20) » ([PDFPageProxy](https://mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/api/draft/module-pdfjsLib-PDFPageProxy.html)).
- `TextContent` contient `items` (mélange de `TextItem` et `TextMarkedContent`), `styles` et `lang` ; `TextItem` expose `str`, `transform`, `fontName`, `width`, `height`, `hasEOL`. `getTextContentParameters` offre `includeMarkedContent` (défaut `false`) et `disableNormalization` (défaut `false`) ([module-pdfjsLib](https://mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/api/draft/module-pdfjsLib.html)).
- Point important : **l'extraction de texte n'exige pas de canvas** — seul le rendu en image en a besoin (déduction directe de la séparation entre les deux exemples officiels).

**Hypothèses d'exécution documentées côté Node**
- Défauts différents en Node, documentés dans les JSDoc de `DocumentInitParameters` : `useSystemFonts` (`true` web / `false` Node), `disableFontFace` (`false` web / `true` Node), `useWorkerFetch` (`true` web / `false` Node), `isOffscreenCanvasSupported` et `isImageDecoderSupported` (`true` web / `false` Node) ([api.js](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/display/api.js), [module-pdfjsLib](https://mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/api/draft/module-pdfjsLib.html)). `cMapUrl`, `standardFontDataUrl` et `wasmUrl` doivent être fournis explicitement ([même doc](https://mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/api/draft/module-pdfjsLib.html)).
- Workers : `if (isNodeJS) { // Workers aren't supported in Node.js, force-disabling them there. this.#isWorkerDisabled = true; ... }`, avec repli sur un « fake worker » chargé par `import()` dynamique et un `LoopbackPort` ([api.js](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/display/api.js)). Concrètement : **tout tourne sur le thread principal**.
- Sélection de factories : en GENERIC + Node, `NodeCanvasFactory`, `NodeFilterFactory`, `NodeBinaryDataFactory` remplacent leurs équivalents DOM ([api.js](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/display/api.js)).
- `src/display/node_utils.js` utilise `process.getBuiltinModule("fs/promises")` et `process.getBuiltinModule("module")` (pour `createRequire`), et charge `@napi-rs/canvas`, décrit comme fournissant aussi les polyfills `DOMMatrix` et `Path2D` ([node_utils.js](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/display/node_utils.js)).
- `@napi-rs/canvas` est une **dépendance optionnelle** de `pdfjs-dist` (`^1.0.0`) ; `type: "module"`, entrée `build/pdf.mjs`, champ `browser` neutralisant `fs`, `url`, `http`, `https`, `canvas` ; version publiée 6.2.108 et **`engines.node: ">=22.13.0 || >=24"`** ([registre npm](https://registry.npmjs.org/pdfjs-dist/latest) ; même champ `engines` dans le [package.json amont](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/package.json)).

## 2. Ce que cela implique pour Bun (inférence, pas doctrine officielle)

Aucune source officielle PDF.js ne mentionne Bun : les issues du dépôt remontées par la recherche pour « Bun » sont des faux positifs sans rapport ([recherche d'issues](https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/issues?q=Bun)). **Il n'existe donc pas de position officielle sur Bun** ; ce qui suit est déduit des hypothèses ci-dessus.

- **Détection d'environnement** : `isNodeJS` repose sur `process + "" === "[object process]"`. Si Bun ne reproduit pas exactement cette sérialisation, PDF.js se croit dans un navigateur et tente des chemins DOM. Je n'ai pas vérifié empiriquement le comportement de Bun sur ce point — **incertain**.
- **`process.getBuiltinModule`** : requis par `node_utils.js`. Bun a suivi cette API (issue [oven-sh/bun#12161](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/issues/12161) ; les notes de 1.4 indiquent que `require()`, `import()` et `process.getBuiltinModule()` renvoient le même objet pour les modules natifs, [Bun 1.4](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/issues/28792)). Sur des Bun plus anciens, un tiers rapporte `process.getBuiltinModule undefined` avec une erreur `DOMMatrix` ([pdf-parse#73](https://github.com/mehmet-kozan/pdf-parse/issues/73)) — source non officielle, mais cohérente avec le code amont ; le même symptôme est documenté officiellement pour Node < 22.3/20.16 ([pdf.js#19150](https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/issues/19150)).
- **DOMMatrix / Path2D / OffscreenCanvas / ImageDecoder** : la doc de compatibilité Bun ne les liste pas ([Bun – Node.js APIs](https://bun.com/docs/runtime/nodejs-apis)). PDF.js désactive OffscreenCanvas et ImageDecoder par défaut en Node, mais s'appuie sur `@napi-rs/canvas` pour `DOMMatrix`/`Path2D` ([node_utils.js](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/display/node_utils.js)) : si la détection Node échoue sous Bun, ces polyfills ne sont pas installés.
- **Modules natifs** : le seul rapport Bun ↔ pdfjs-dist trouvé est [oven-sh/bun#9711](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/issues/9711) (crash `dyld: missing symbol called`, mars 2024, Bun 1.0.36, fermé « not planned », sans contournement documenté). Ancien et probablement lié au binding canvas natif — **preuve faible aujourd'hui**.
- **Version Node déclarée** : `engines >=22.13.0 || >=24` ; Bun ne satisfait pas ce champ au sens strict (il n'est pas Node), donc ce n'est qu'un indicateur du niveau de fonctionnalités attendu.

**Recommandation pratique déduite** : pour de l'extraction de texte sous Bun, importer `pdfjs-dist/legacy/build/pdf.mjs`, passer les données en `Uint8Array`, fournir `cMapUrl`/`standardFontDataUrl` (et `wasmUrl` en v6), et ne pas installer `@napi-rs/canvas` si l'on ne fait pas de rendu. Un projet tiers, `unpdf`, se présente explicitement comme un build de PDF.js portable sur tous les runtimes dont Bun ([unjs/unpdf](https://github.com/unjs/unpdf)) — alternative, non endossée par Mozilla.

## 3. Limites de cette recherche

- Les contenus GitHub raw ont été résumés par un modèle intermédiaire : les extraits de code sont fidèles dans l'esprit mais pas garantis mot pour mot (notamment le bloc `#setupFakeWorker`).
- Le dépôt miroir `mozilla/pdfjs-dist` sur `master` renvoie une version obsolète (3.2.146, dépendance optionnelle `canvas`) alors que npm publie 6.2.108 avec `@napi-rs/canvas` — **divergence de sources** ; j'ai retenu le registre npm comme faisant foi.
- Le wiki « Frequently Questioned Answers » n'a pas pu être lu (chargement en erreur côté GitHub).
